claims.quote: Inform patients also that the central nervous system depressant effects of allopurinol tablets may be additive to those of alcohol and other CNS depressants.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote explicitly states allopurinol's CNS depressant effects may be additive with alcohol, matching the claim's co-exposure and uncertain 'may' wording.

claims.text: The label reports drowsiness, somnolence and dizziness in patients taking allopurinol tablets
claims.quote: Drowsiness, somnolence and dizziness have been reported in patients taking allopurinol tablets [see Adverse Reactions (6) ] .
claims.judgeRationale: The quote reports only allopurinol monotherapy effects without alcohol co-exposure or explicit uncertainty about the pair, so the uncertain pair stance is unsupported.

claims.text: In 150 gout patients starting allopurinol, alcohol drinking linked to raised transaminases
claims.quote: One hundred and fifty patients with gout and normal baseline serum aminotransferases initiated on allopurinol were followed prospectively over three visits. A total of 32 (21.5%) drank alcohol, 43 (28.9%) were obese, and 11 (7.3%) had metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Thirty (20.0%) developed raised AST/ALT levels during follow-up, the majority (86.7%) being mild, while none were severe. Multivariate analysis revealed that alcohol consumption (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.52, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-8.79) and statin nonuse (adjusted OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.04-11.17) were independent predictors of raised transaminase levels.

claims.text: Alcohol consumption predicted raised transaminase levels
claims.quote: Multivariate analysis revealed that alcohol consumption (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.52, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-8.79) and statin nonuse (adjusted OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.04-11.17) were independent predictors of raised transaminase levels.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote reports alcohol consumption alone as an independent predictor of raised transaminases without assessing alcohol combined with allopurinol, so it does not support a pair-interaction claim.
